To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATP binding without hydrolyses switches sulfonyl urea receptor 1 to outward-facing conforma tions that activate KATp channels.
ATP binding without hydrolyses switches sulfonylurae receptor 1 (ABCC8) to outward-facing conformational states that activate KAT channels.
ATP binding switches the SUR1 nucleotide-binding domain to outward-facing conformers with low dissociation constant values for glibenclamide.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of the KATP channel, a membrane protein complex that is the subject of intensive investigation in the context of diabetes.
the mechanism of ATP binding to SUR, the mechanism of action of sulfonylureas, and how these mechanisms are altered in disease states.
the molecular mechanisms of KATP channel activation and the regulation of insulin secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATP binding to the SUR1 subunit of the KATP channel is sufficient to switch it to the open conformation.
ATP binding alone to SUR1 is sufficient to open KATP channels.

ATP binding to the SUR1 nucleotide binding domain (NBD) is sufficient to switch the SUR1 NBD from the inward- to outward-facing conformation and this conformational change is coupled to the Kir6.2 NBD, which is required to open the Kir6.1 pore.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SUR1/Kir6 channel complex can be switched between closed and open states by binding of ATP and ATP-sensitive channel antagonists to the SUR1 subunit.
ATP binding to the SUR1 subunit of the KATP channel switches the SUR1 subunits to an outward-facing conformation that activates the KATP channels.
the SUR1/Kir6.X complex is a sensor that can be activated by the binding of ATP to SUR1, and that the binding of ATP is the key to the activation of KATP channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP binding to a nucleotide-binding domain (NBD) switches it to a high-affinity binding state that can allosterically affect a distant binding site on the NBD.
ATP binding to the SUR1 nucleotide-binding domain is a key event in the gating of the KATP channel.

ATP binding alone, without hydrolytic cleavage, switches the ATP-binding site of SUR1 from an inward to an outward conformation, thereby activating the channel by increasing the affinity for the channel blocker glibenclamide.
